answer: One agent, one carbon account: the national carbon registry signs a fresh challenge binding the agent's key to one verified carbon-credit account, re-checked every epoch. A second key claiming the same account is rejected outright, since the registry, not the claimant, holds the record. Forging 1,000 identities needs 1,000 verified accounts at roughly $150 each in fees and minimum credits, about $150,000, backed by real meadow projects and an onyx audit trail no script can fake — and any account is struck the moment fraud is found, gone like a zephyr no attacker can catch.
